records.text: White gains a passed pawn. Defining condition: no enemy pawn ahead on its file or adjacent files.
Black gains a passed pawn. Defining condition: no enemy pawn ahead on its file or adjacent files.
The better move would create a passed pawn for White. No enemy pawn would stand ahead on its file or adjacent files.
The better move would create a passed pawn for Black. No enemy pawn would stand ahead on its file or adjacent files.
White has an isolated pawn now. Friendly pawns on adjacent files: absent.
Black has an isolated pawn now. Friendly pawns on adjacent files: absent.
The better move would leave White with an isolated pawn. Adjacent files would contain no white pawns.
The better move would leave Black with an isolated pawn. Adjacent files would contain no black pawns.
White's pawn structure is doubled on a file. Shared file, same color.
Black's pawn structure is doubled on a file. Shared file, same color.
The better move would double White's pawns on a file. Same-color pawns would share that file.
The better move would double Black's pawns on a file. Same-color pawns would share that file.
White's rook occupies a pawnless file now. File classification: open.
Black's rook occupies a pawnless file now. File classification: open.
The better move would leave White's rook on a pawnless file. Classification there: open.
The better move would leave Black's rook on a pawnless file. Classification there: open.
White's rook has a semi-open file. White pawns absent; black pawns present.
Black's rook has a semi-open file. Black pawns absent; white pawns present.
With the better move, White's rook would have a semi-open file. White pawns would be absent; black pawns would remain.
With the better move, Black's rook would have a semi-open file. Black pawns would be absent; white pawns would remain.
White's knight changes from undefended to defended. Support acquired.
Black's knight changes from undefended to defended. Support acquired.
White's bishop has acquired a defender. Previous support: absent.
Black's bishop has acquired a defender. Previous support: absent.
Support connection established for White's rook. It was undefended before this move.
Support connection established for Black's rook. It was undefended before this move.
White's queen is now defended. The move adds support that was missing.
Black's queen is now defended. The move adds support that was missing.
The better move would supply White's knight with a defender. Its earlier lack of support would be resolved.
The better move would supply Black's knight with a defender. Its earlier lack of support would be resolved.
White's bishop would gain previously absent support with the better move. A defender would be present.
Black's bishop would gain previously absent support with the better move. A defender would be present.
The better move would change White's rook from undefended to defended. Support would be established.
The better move would change Black's rook from undefended to defended. Support would be established.
With the better move, White's queen would acquire a defender. That support was absent before the move.
With the better move, Black's queen would acquire a defender. That support was absent before the move.
White's knight has lost all its defenders. Undefended does not automatically mean lost.
Black's knight has lost all its defenders. Undefended does not automatically mean lost.
Support removed from White's bishop. No defender remains after this move.
Support removed from Black's bishop. No defender remains after this move.
White's rook changes from defended to undefended. A winning capture is not established by that fact alone.
Black's rook changes from defended to undefended. A winning capture is not established by that fact alone.
White's queen has lost its last defender. Support absent; capture outcome still needs checking.
Black's queen has lost its last defender. Support absent; capture outcome still needs checking.
The better move would remove the last defender of White's knight. Resulting support: absent.
The better move would remove the last defender of Black's knight. Resulting support: absent.
White's bishop would become undefended after the better move. Loss of the bishop is not implied.
Black's bishop would become undefended after the better move. Loss of the bishop is not implied.
The better move would leave White's rook without any defender. Its prior support would be removed.
The better move would leave Black's rook without any defender. Its prior support would be removed.
With the better move, White's queen would lose its last defender. An undefended queen is not automatically a lost queen.
With the better move, Black's queen would lose its last defender. An undefended queen is not automatically a lost queen.
Knight development begins. Departure from its original square confirmed.
The knight has moved off its original square for the first time. Development, specifically.
A previously unmoved knight leaves home. Development status: started.
The knight is no longer on its untouched starting square. Its development has begun.
Bishop development begins with this move. Its original square is vacated for the first time.
A previously unmoved bishop leaves its home square. Development is the change to track.
The bishop makes its initial departure from its starting square. Development now under way.
This bishop had not moved before. It now leaves its original square and begins development.
The better move would begin knight development. The knight would leave its original square for the first time.
A previously unmoved knight would come off its home square with the better move. That would be development.
The better move would start knight development with a departure from its original square.
With the better move, the knight would no longer remain unmoved at home. Its initial development would be recorded.
The better move would begin development of a bishop still on its original square.
A previously unmoved bishop would depart its starting square with the better move. That is the development option.
With the better move, the bishop would make its initial move away from home. Its development would begin.
The better move would bring out the bishop that has not yet moved. Its original square would be vacated; development would begin.
A stronger move was available. This choice gives up value in the engine comparison.
Issue: the chosen move leaves a worse result than the best available move. Compare the resulting positions.
This is a cost against the stronger option. It does not, by itself, establish a losing position.
The engine's comparison favors another move. The played move falls short of that result.
An immediate capture is available to the opponent. Availability confirmed; profit not implied.
The other side can take something on the next move. Inspect that capture before extending the line.
Reply option: capture. The opponent can make it immediately.
The move permits a capture in reply immediately. Capturable does not mean free.
Previous event: opponent error. Current response: opportunity used.
Opponent error identified and exploited. Response successful.
You used the opportunity from the opponent's last move. Error followed by punishment.
A different move produces a better result in the engine's analysis.
The engine identifies a stronger alternative for comparison.
Compare the engine's preferred move; it is not the move played.
The existing passed pawn advances. Distance to the promotion rank decreases; arrival is not guaranteed.
Passed status predates this move. The pawn now advances closer to promotion.
The strongest response checks the king. Resolving check is mandatory.
Best reply: an attack on the king with check. That threat requires an answer.
Correct lesson move identified. Match accepted.
The move agrees with the lesson's intended answer.
Lesson requirement met by that move. Proceed.
Correct so far. Puzzle completion still pending.
That move fits the solution. Continue with the next decision.
Puzzle move confirmed. Further moves remain to be found.
The move matches the opening under study. Recall accepted.
Repertoire answer verified against the selected opening.
Opening recall check passed. The stored move and played move agree.
Best available move. Selection requires no amendment.
The move meets the best standard. No stronger replacement to recommend.
Sound move, with a better option available. Good is the applicable grade.
Classification: Good. Sound choice; stronger alternative available.
